why: Compare from both ends: a palindrome check is two pointers walking toward each other, here with a twist that each pointer first skips characters that are not letters or digits, and the comparison ignores case.
hints: You could build the filtered, lower-cased string and compare it with its reverse. Can you do it without building anything?
Put i at the start and j at the end. Advance i past non-alphanumeric characters, retreat j likewise, then compare s[i] and s[j] case-insensitively.
Loop while i < j: skip, compare, move both inward. Any mismatch returns false; meeting in the middle returns true. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Digits count: '0P' is not a palindrome.
A string with no letters or digits (or an empty string) is a palindrome.
Keep the skip loops bounded by i < j so they cannot run off the string.
